chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about sleeping in the Sacred Masjid and the Masjid of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, so where would the people sleep?'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sleep in the Masjid al-Haram and Masjid al-Nabi according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Muawiya ibn Wahb queries Imam al-Sadiq (AS) regarding the permissibility of sleeping in the Masjid al-Haram and Masjid al-Nabi. The Imam’s affirmative response, accompanied by the rhetorical question 'Where else would people sleep?', underscores the practical necessity of utilizing these sacred spaces for rest during long prayers or stays, thereby validating the mosque as a multi-functional sanctuary for the community. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly view that the sanctity of the mosque does not preclude its use for essential human needs like sleep, provided general decorum is maintained.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Muawiya Bin Wahab who said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the sleeping in the Sacred Masjid, and the Masjid of the Prophet<sup>saww</sup>. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So where would the people sleep?’
en.sarwar: 10. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus from Mu‘awiyah ibn Wahab who has said the following: “
I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, Alayhi al-Salam, about sleeping in Masjid al-Haram and Masjid of the Holy prophet. He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, they can do so, where else can people sleep?”’
